'''''Leonurus''''' ('''motherwort''') is a genus of [[flowering plant]]s in the family [[Lamiaceae]]. It is native to Europe and Asia, naturalized in New Zealand, [[Hawaii]], [[New Caledonia]], and much of North and South America.<ref name=wcsp>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=109490 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref><ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=117993 Flora of China Vol. 17 Page 162 <big>益母草属</big> yi mu cao shu ''Leonurus'' Linnaeus, Sp. Pl. 2: 584. 1753. ]</ref><ref>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/gen.php?genere=Leonurus Altervista Flora Italiana, Genere  ''Leonurus''] includes photos + European distribution maps</ref><ref>[http://bonap.net/NAPA/TaxonMaps/Genus/County/Leonurus Biota of North America Program 2013 county distribution maps]</ref>

''[[Leonurus japonicus]]'' is one of the [[Chinese herbology#50 fundamental herbs|50 fundamental herbs]] used in [[traditional Chinese medicine]].

Species are sometimes confused with the related genus ''[[Leonotis]].''
